g.text: OpenCode-native controls: what each layer can and cannot do
Hooks and permissions are policy and UX. Only the outer boundary changes what the agent is physically able to reach.
real credential never enters · network deny-by-default · workspace is the only host data
root/sudo inside is fine here, because the boundary is outside the agent
await ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", (e) => { if (risky(e)) throw new Error("blocked") })
approving "always" writes a durable project-scoped allow rule
review saved approvals; a deny rule cannot be overridden by one
Hooks are in-process guardrails, not a sandbox. A project can ship .opencode/plugins, skills and AGENTS.md; run untrusted repos inside the isolation boundary.
